name: The chief priests, and the watch at the sepulchre
charge: Paying the soldiers large money to report a lie about the resurrection
summary: The day after the preparation the chief priests and Pharisees came to Pilate, called Christ a deceiver, and asked that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, because they remembered his saying that after three days he would rise; Pilate gave them a watch, and they sealed the stone and set it (Matthew 27:62-66). When some of the watch came into the city and told the chief priests all the things that were done, the priests assembled with the elders, took counsel, and gave large money to the soldiers to say that the disciples came by night and stole him away while they slept (Matthew 28:11-13).
offenseFull: They remembered the saying better than the disciples did. That is the weight of the request: the men who had him put to death were the men who took his words about the third day seriously enough to post a guard against them. There was an earthquake, and the angel of the Lord came down and rolled back the stone and sat on it, and the keepers shook and became as dead men, and the angel told the women he was not there, for he was risen as he said (Matthew 28:1-6). At that point the matter was settled in front of witnesses, and the men who had asked for the guard could have conceded it. They did not. They assembled, took counsel, and bought the report they had set the watch to prevent (Matthew 28:11-13). Men love darkness rather than light, because their deeds are evil (John 3:19).

The money had a reason behind it. A soldier who lost a prisoner under his watch answered for it with his own life, which is why the priests added that if it came to the governor’s ears they would persuade him and secure them (Matthew 28:14). So the soldiers were bought with money and with a promise of protection from the same men who had just been shown that the promise was worth nothing, since they had made a covenant with death and an agreement with hell, saying the overflowing scourge would not come to them (Isaiah 28:15). Never trust an enemy, whatever the terms (Sirach 12:10). The bargain itself broke the law twice over, against raising a false report and against bearing false witness (Exodus 23:1; Exodus 20:16).
judgmentFull: The soldiers took the money and did as they were taught, and that saying was commonly reported among the Jews until the day the account was written (Matthew 28:15). No sentence on the chief priests, on the elders, or on the soldiers is recorded in the passage. What is recorded is the bargain, with their names attached to it, in a book that has outlived every copy of the story they bought.

The report also could not hold, because of how the resurrection was shown. God raised him the third day and showed him openly, not to all the people, but to witnesses chosen before, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead (Acts 10:40-41). He was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve, and after that of above five hundred brethren at once, most of whom were still alive when Paul wrote it down (1 Corinthians 15:5-6). He showed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs over forty days (Acts 1:3). A crucifixion was a public thing in that city, and so was the darkness and the earthquake that went with this one, so the men who were paid to say they had slept through the one event everyone was talking about were given a story that could not survive the witnesses. The standing rule on such a report is written: a false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaks lies shall not escape (Proverbs 19:5).

text.text: Now the next day, that followed the day of the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate,
Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again.

Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first.
Pilate said unto them, Ye have a watch: go your way, make it as sure as ye can.
So they went, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch.
Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done.
And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave large money unto the soldiers,
Saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.
In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.
And, behold, there was a great earthquake: for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it.
His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow:
And for fear of him the keepers did shake, and became as dead men.
And the angel answered and said unto the women, Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified.
He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
And if this come to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him, and secure you.

Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves:
Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.
Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.
Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day.
Him God raised up the third day, and shewed him openly;
Not to all the people, but unto witnesses chosen before of God, even to us, who did eat and drink with him after he rose from the dead.
And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve:
After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep.
To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days, and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God:
A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall not escape.
